scope: Exposed-161 cohort only (manifest 7036f848, cases 5f332b15). The held-out Q2 cohort (manifest 28063dd5...) and every Q2 path, branch and report were not read, scanned or referenced.

candidate.commit: 1673ec5d (classified at branch head 1b41fd05; rule bytes unchanged)

inputs.case_packets: /home/claude/run-r161/captures/cases-v4 (old/new sources and diff.patch; source bindings equal to the b2a2800f receipt per detector-iteration-20261126.json)

method.classification: One reviewer read each non-hit from the advisory CWE list (manifest), the in-language non-test fix diff and the old-side source around the changed lines. Vulnerability class follows what the fix does where it differs from the CWE (for example, a CWE-89 advisory fixed by an admin check is authz). Every lane and reason is a judgment from reading the code; no proposed rule was written or tested.
method.flagged_anywhere_rescan: The b2a2800f receipt stores only aggregate file_hits (50), so to recover per-case file-level alerts the old side of all 158 scannable exposed packets was rescanned once under flock /tmp/recall-replay.lock. Each scan used the frozen b2a2800f rules, the profile argv (profileArgv) and the harness exports sarifFindings/parseHunks/scoreCase, with no new logic. The rescan reproduces the receipt exactly: 40/40 hunk hits case for case, 0 mismatches, 50 file hits, 0 engine errors. Scratch SARIF stayed in /tmp and was deleted.
method.pattern_recoverable_estimate: true when best_lane is pattern and the proposed pattern alert would sit on an old-hunk line (pattern_alert_in_old_hunk_likely), or for outside_hunk cases where the existing alert is at this vulnerability's sink (recoverable by a scoring change only). This is an upper bound: precision controls and the fixed-side residual limit have not been run.

miss_reasons.no_rule: No rule for this class or language
miss_reasons.interprocedural: A rule exists, but the flow crosses functions or files (needs interprocedural analysis)
miss_reasons.sink_unmodeled: The sink is behind framework/ORM dispatch or has a shape the patterns do not model
miss_reasons.not_pattern: Not expressible as a pattern (logic, authz, configuration, sanitizer/deny-list completeness)
miss_reasons.outside_hunk: The alert lands outside the fixed hunk (same vulnerability flagged elsewhere in the same file)
miss_reasons.no_source_change: No in-language source change, or unknown

lanes.codeql: CodeQL interprocedural (python, javascript, ruby, go, java, csharp)
lanes.native_sast: Native SAST (language-native taint tool; used for PHP, which CodeQL does not cover)
lanes.none: None (needs a human or a test)

flagged_anywhere_in_file.note: family_relevant counts the receipt file_hit definition: an alert of the advisory family in a changed file on the old side, minus the hunk hits (50 - 40 = 10). Only 4 of the 10 are the same vulnerability flagged at its sink; the other 6 are unrelated alerts in a large file.

top5_recoverable_buckets.rationale: Add DB-wrapper and builder sinks (ADOdb Execute/GetOne/GetAll, Rails finder taking a whole params hash, go-sqlbuilder Select with a Sprintf quoted %s). The SQL text is on the deleted line. GHSA-jjgq is excluded because its $db->query sink is outside the hunks.
Model Symfony $request->get()/query/request bags and framework-bound Go form structs as sources; both pimcore cases concatenate the value into a hand-quoted condition fragment on the deleted line.

Widen python.parameter-path-join-without-containment operand shapes ($BASE / ($A + $P), $BASE / $P[...]), and stop treating a custom tar members= filter whose check is startswith() without os.sep as a sanitizer.

Already flagged at the secure_popen sink; the fix edits the sanitizer above it. Needs no rule change, only a scoring decision (trace or sanitizer-span attribution), which Codex owns. The same mechanism covers GHSA-4h97 (sql) and GHSA-vj3g (path): 4 cases in total.

C# ProcessStartInfo{FileName="cmd.exe", Arguments=$"/C ...{x}"} with a non-literal interpolation, and git subcommands taking a variable positional argument without a "--" end-of-options marker. Tied at 2 with five other buckets; see tie_note.

tie_note: Six class x reason x lane buckets tie at 2 recoverable cases: injection-command/outside_hunk (ranked 4: no rule work), injection-command/no_rule (ranked 5), injection-command/source_unmodeled (GHSA-6qjf %x interpolation, GHSA-mc7w process.argv), injection-sql/no_rule (GHSA-mhwp Ruby ^$ anchors, GHSA-vmw2 C# SQL text), injection-code/no_rule (GHSA-6m8w rego.Query, GHSA-8gqp Nashorn without --no-java) and deserialization/no_rule (GHSA-2pm6 misspelled allowed_classes, GHSA-2fmj case-sensitive phar:// check).
proposals_for_codex: Scoring (Codex-owned, not implemented): the 4 same-vulnerability outside-hunk cases (GHSA-4h97, GHSA-73wf, GHSA-qcpp, GHSA-vj3g) have the alert at the sink while the fix edits a sanitizer or validator upstream. A pre-registered secondary metric that credits a same-file family alert on the fixed flow (or trace_hit when the SARIF carries a dataflow step in the hunk) would count them without any rule change. It must be pre-registered and reported apart from hunk_hits.

Join (Codex-owned): the 13 codeql-lane and 4 native_sast-lane cases are where the native-to-pattern fingerprint join would add recall. Their CodeQL alerts would mostly land at the sink, outside the fix hunk, so the same scoring question applies.
caveats: One reviewer, diff-level reading. Reasons and lanes are judgments; borderline calls are noted in each rationale.
The pattern-recoverable count is an upper bound: no rule was written, and precision controls and the 10% fixed-side residual tolerance (limit 0.48 per hit) were not evaluated.
GHSA-mrq8/GHSA-6vmq and GHSA-r8g5/GHSA-x843 share a fix commit, so each pair counts twice.
Five non-hits are not scored misses: 3 coverage_incomplete and 2 unknown (no old-side source; no in-language source change).
access_record: /home/claude/run-ra.sh and /home/claude/run-pp/full-b2a2800f.sh were opened only to identify which runs used held-out manifests; both were then avoided, and no run-ra or run-pp results, checkpoints or captures were read.
